summary:
The build matches the design and its four critique dispositions. I re-ran the checks myself; nothing that should send the build back was found.

**What changed:** 5 test files, one comment in ScanResult.cs (remark at :205-208), and two docs. Scanner.cs is byte-identical to HEAD.

**What I ran on this PC:**
- **Slice classes, engine's TEMP (C:\WINDOWS\TEMP):** 114/114 passed.
  - The three Windows\Temp lines read 'kept 4 of 7 ... moved: <root>, plain, links'.
  - The ProgramData line read 'C:\ProgramData\fsa-tests\<guid>: kept 7 of 7; 7 of 7 ... moved: none'.
  - The LOCALAPPDATA line read 'kept 7 of 7 ... moved: none'.
- **Full suite:** 804/804 passed.
- **Class run under the owner's TEMP (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp):** 6/6, with the same lines.
- **Cleanup:** C:\ProgramData\fsa-tests had 0 entries before and after every run.
- **Fitness op=check:** 87 rules, every declared rule holds.
- **rules-parity:** AGREE 18 facts / 22 twinned / 48 patterns, under both pwsh and powershell.exe.
- **Mutation:** I replaced Scanner.cs:340 with `if (false)`, which widens the correction everywhere. The new Fact went red with 'kept 4 of 7 ... a correction fired outside %SystemRoot%'. I restored the file (hash equal, git diff empty), touched it, and the owner-TEMP run above was built from the restored source.

**Measured for O-010:**
- A child process with ProgramData stripped (or ALLUSERSPROFILE, SystemDrive, or SystemRoot/windir, each alone) still resolves GetFolderPath(CommonApplicationData) to C:\ProgramData.
- With all six location variables stripped at once, it comes back blank. ChooseProgramDataTestsRoot then refuses it as 'it is blank', so it fails closed, as designed.

**Probe of the create refusal:** a folder in my own %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp with a deny-AD ACE makes Directory.CreateDirectory throw UnauthorizedAccessException. The new refusal test feeds only the IOException shape (a parent that is a file). That leaves the ACL branch Q-210 ruled on without a test. It is filed as an extra.

**Docs:** the reflection guard, the prose pin and the SL-097 doc hold what M1, M2, m1 and m2 asked. The doc reports spike #3 as measured, and 'falsified' appears nowhere.

The index shows one build attempt and no loop.

Second round: Second pass, reading as someone trying to break the change. I found one new weakness, filed as an extra (m2). Nothing here sends the build back.

**What I checked:**
- **Inputs to the new root-chooser and the create refusal:** padding, relative and drive-relative paths, under-Windows spellings, a blank Windows folder.
- **Create-refusal wrap:** every exception the creation call can throw (path too long, directory not found and plain I/O errors are wrapped with the inner exception kept; the compression refusal passes through).
- **Reflection guard:** a lambda body is not counted as a test, a test made static or non-public goes red by name, overloads go red, and a derived Fact or Theory attribute is counted.
- **Prose pin:** each phrase it requires is new in this diff ('Windows 10' and 'SL-097' were absent at 2fc73e1). The files are CRLF (the new doc is LF), with no byte-order mark, and every pinned phrase sits on one line.
- **Parallel runs:** no other Core test scans or lists C:\ProgramData. The only ProgramData uses are string-only (ContainerLayerStore.Locate, UnreadableRows paths), so nothing in the suite races the new %ProgramData% tree.

**New finding (m2):** the M1 prose pin bans one spelling of the claim critique M1 retracted. It forbids 'falsified' in the SL-097 record and nothing else. So a record that drops the +30 s re-scan bullet, or restates the design's own wrong wording ('shows no under-count'), stays green.

findings.claim:
The new create-refusal test does not feed the shape Q-210 ruled on: a tests root refused by its ACL.
- The test uses a tests root whose parent is a file, so the inner exception is an IOException.
- I measured on this PC that an ACL refusal of Directory.CreateDirectory throws UnauthorizedAccessException. I used a folder in my own %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp with a deny-AD ACE: 'Access to the path ... is denied'.
- UnauthorizedAccessException does not derive from IOException. No other test raises it through TempTree.CreateRoot.
- So a mutant that narrows CreateRoot's filter to `when (e is IOException)` survives the whole suite, and the C:\Windows\Temp access-denied case Q-210 named would be a bare exception again.

The code is right today (TempTree.cs:111 catches both types). Only the proof is missing. The design marked case 10 as not material, so this is backlog work, not a send-back.
findings.evidence: tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/TempTreeTests.cs:54-67 (feeds a file-as-parent root and asserts IsAssignableFrom<IOException>); tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/TempTree.cs:111 `catch (Exception e) when (e is UnauthorizedAccessException or IOException)`; my probe: icacls /deny <me>:(AD) on a %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp folder, then [IO.Directory]::CreateDirectory under it -> System.UnauthorizedAccessException
findings.fix:
Add a second refusal test with no system ACL change:
- Inside a default TempTree, make a folder X and deny it FILE_ADD_SUBDIRECTORY with the existing helper, tree.Deny(X, 0x4). TempTree.Dispose already removes deny ACEs first.
- Assert that new TempTree(Path.Combine(X, "fsa-tests")) throws InvalidOperationException containing 'Could not create', with InnerException of type UnauthorizedAccessException.

findings.claim:
TheMeasuredLastAccessLimitIsWrittenWhereTheTreeSaidUnmeasured guards the SL-097 record against critique M1 by banning one word, 'falsified'. Its only other assertion on the record is that it contains 'Windows 10'.

M1's substance is that the +30 s un-back-dated re-scan must be recorded as the existing under-count gap (3 folders counted out with nothing moved). The design's own wrong wording was 'shows no under-count', which is not the banned word. So the test stays green if the record:
- restates that wording, or
- calls the limit 'disproved' or 'refuted', or
- deletes the re-scan section entirely.

The builder's O-012 account ('A test pins all of it') and the engine's 'proved' both rest on a mutant that inserted exactly 'falsified'. The record is correct today; only the guard is narrower than claimed. M1 itself asked for no test, so this goes to the backlog.
findings.evidence: tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/LastAccessRuleCorpusTests.cs:162-163 are the only assertions on `record`. The design's retracted wording (outside_claims and case 12's why) is '+30 s ... moves nothing and shows no under-count'. The correct sentence in docs/design/SL-097-last-access-outside-the-windows-folder.md, section 'A re-scan of the same C:\Windows\Temp tree', reads '...were counted out although none moved. That is the gap ...'.
findings.fix: Pin the correct statement positively instead of banning one word. Add `Assert.Contains("counted out although none moved", record);`, a phrase that sits on one line of the doc today. Optionally also add `Assert.DoesNotContain("no under-count", record, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase);`.
findings.class_of: spellings of the retracted re-scan claim that the prose pin does not ban

obligations.evidence: tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests.cs:109-131 builds the 7-folder nested tree under ChooseProgramDataTestsRoot(GetFolderPath(CommonApplicationData), ...), back-dates it 48 h through BackDateAndScan and asserts asked == 7, kept == 7 and still-old == kept. My run printed 'C:\ProgramData\fsa-tests\306e2f3b...: kept 7 of 7; 7 of 7 folders still at least 47 h old; moved: none'.

In my class runs the same invocation printed the Windows\Temp lines 'kept 4 of 7 ... moved: <root>, plain, links' for all three spellings, plus the LOCALAPPDATA line 'moved: none'. Those Facts assert kept == still-old, so a green class run means parents did move there.

Ran under TEMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP (114/114) and under TEMP=%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp (6/6). Both printed a C:\ProgramData\fsa-tests path with kept 7 of 7. In the code the root comes only from GetFolderPath (LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests.cs:112-114), never from TEMP.
Three green runs of mine (slice classes, full suite, owner-TEMP class run), on top of the builder's three. The ProgramData line was 'kept 7 of 7 ... moved: none' every time.
InTree (LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests.cs:144-150) asserts the <guid> tree is gone after Dispose. C:\ProgramData\fsa-tests held 0 entries before and after each of my runs (new names: 0).

- ScanResult.cs:205-208 states the measured limit, naming SL-097 and Windows 10.
- docs/design/SL-096-last-access-under-windows-temp.md limits rewritten to point at SL-097.
- docs/design/SL-097-last-access-outside-the-windows-folder.md exists.
- All three are pinned by LastAccessRuleCorpusTests.TheMeasuredLastAccessLimitIsWrittenWhereTheTreeSaidUnmeasured (:143-164), which passed.
- A grep of src, docs and tests finds no remaining 'unmeasured' next to ProgramData or ProgramFiles.
Full suite 804/804. Fitness op=check: 87 rules, every declared rule holds. eng/rules-parity.ps1: AGREE 18 facts <- 22 twinned, 48 patterns, exit 0 in both pwsh and powershell.exe.

TempTreeRootTests.cs:68-103 feeds ChooseProgramDataTestsRoot blank, whitespace, relative, drive-relative and three under-Windows spellings, plus a blank or relative Windows folder. Each is refused by name. The comparison uses the same GetFolderPath(Windows), NormalizeRoot and IsAtOrUnder as Scanner.WindowsFolderFromEnvironment and Scanner.cs:340.

In this engine shell the Fact printed C:\ProgramData\fsa-tests\<guid>.
- A child pwsh with ProgramData stripped (or ALLUSERSPROFILE, SystemDrive, or SystemRoot/windir, each alone) still resolves CommonApplicationData to C:\ProgramData.
- With all six location variables stripped it returns blank. ChooseProgramDataTestsRoot refuses that as 'it is blank': red with a cause, never a false pass.
The Fact is in LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests.cs with a stock [Fact], no Trait, no filter clause and no separate class. It ran in the default full suite.

- The SL-097 doc's re-scan section reports +180 s and +20 min re-back-dated scans moving again, and the +30 s un-back-dated scan counting 3 out with nothing moved, as the existing gap.
- No 'falsified' anywhere; the pin asserts DoesNotContain.
- ScanResult.cs:201 'counted out even when nothing moved' and SL-096 'It is wrong when nothing moved' are still present.

LastAccessRuleCorpusTests.cs:97 pins nameof(InProgramDataNoKeptFolderMovesItsParent). Lines 102-110 assert that the class's DeclaredOnly methods carrying a FactAttribute (inherit: true, so Theory counts) equal the pinned list exactly.

The SL-097 doc's section 'If the %ProgramData% Fact goes red' restates the losing branch as a re-design: own class, Trait, FsaDefaultTestFilter clause, OptInTraitTests pin, shared helpers and a wider filter. Nothing was made opt-in.

TempTree.cs:105-118: CreateRoot wraps only Directory.CreateDirectory, catching UnauthorizedAccessException and IOException. The message names the root and the cause and is true for every caller. The compression refusal at :119-127 is unwrapped. Only the IOException branch is fed by a test (see m1).

cases.evidence: InProgramDataNoKeptFolderMovesItsParent builds the 7-folder nested tree under <CommonApplicationData>\fsa-tests\<guid>, back-dates it 48 h and checks every entry is old before the scan. It asserts asked == 7 (every keep-open granted). Run: kept 7 of 7, moved: none.

The control works because the class runs together, not through an assertion in the ProgramData Fact. A green class run or full suite requires the Windows\Temp Facts (kept == still-old) to pass, which needs parents to move. My runs showed 'moved: <root>, plain, links' beside the ProgramData 'moved: none'. A single-Fact filter run has no control, and the doc says so.
I ran the class under TEMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP and under TEMP=%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp. Both gave the C:\ProgramData\fsa-tests root with kept 7 of 7. The root is taken only from GetFolderPath.
Three green runs of mine plus the builder's three. No red on the ProgramData line.
InTree asserts the <guid> tree is gone. C:\ProgramData\fsa-tests had 0 entries before and after each of my runs.

TheMeasuredLastAccessLimitIsWrittenWhereTheTreeSaidUnmeasured reads the real ScanResult.cs, the SL-096 doc and the SL-097 doc. It asserts the old phrases are gone, SL-097 and Windows 10 are present, and the re-scan gap sentences survive.
Full suite 804/804, Fitness op=check passes all 87 rules, rules-parity AGREEs in both shells.

Not a standing test. My mutation run replaced Scanner.cs:340 with `if (false)`, and InProgramDataNoKeptFolderMovesItsParent went red at 'kept 4 of 7 ... a correction fired outside %SystemRoot%'. Restored with hash equal.

TempTreeRootTests.AProgramDataThatIsNotUsableIsRefusedByName and AProgramDataRootIsRefusedWhenTheWindowsFolderCannotBeTold feed blank, whitespace, relative, drive-relative and under-Windows values (and a bad Windows folder) straight into ChooseProgramDataTestsRoot.

TempTreeTests.ATestsRootThatCannotBeCreatedIsRefusedByName feeds a root whose parent is a file, which gives an IOException. The case's shape, an ACL refusal, gives UnauthorizedAccessException (I measured it). That branch of CreateRoot's filter is reached by no test (finding m1). The case was marked not material in the design.

Deferred, no test. The reason still holds: a standard user cannot create a tree in %ProgramFiles% (1 of 10,442 folders write-grantable), and a standing probe would move real install folders. The verdict is recorded in the SL-097 doc.

Deferred, no test. The design's 'why' misread spike #3 (critique M1), but the SL-097 doc now reports it correctly as the existing 'counted out even when nothing moved' gap. Nothing the result depends on changed (Scanner.cs untouched), so the deferral holds.

drift: For the next reader, the design's recalled claim is now measured. GetFolderPath(CommonApplicationData) survives a host that strips ProgramData, ALLUSERSPROFILE or SystemDrive one at a time. With six location variables stripped together it returns blank, and the Fact then fails closed with 'it is blank'.
